transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. 

Um, what brings me in is... well, I hardly eat right anymore. It's probably nothing to worry too much about, just... some days it's just coffee and maybe a piece of bread. I try to do better, but my pants are hanging pretty loose on me now. I don't want to make a big fuss out of it, but... is that the right kind of thing to talk to you about? Am I answering your question okay?
Have you noticed a significant change in your appetite or experienced weight loss recently?

Yes, sir... um, like I was just saying, I guess my appetite has changed a whole lot. I hope you don't think I'm doing it on purpose or that I'm trying to be difficult, I just... I really don't feel hungry at all. 

So yeah, mostly it's just the coffee and a piece of bread some days. And I definitely lost weight, since I have to pull my belt so tight just to keep my pants up now. I know I should be eating better meals, and I'm really trying, I promise. Does that answer your question okay?
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that activities you once liked doing now feel uninteresting or meaningless?

Well, sir... I guess, maybe a little bit? I hope that's alright to say. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around being lazy all day, but... yeah. 

I used to really like going for walks by the lake, you know? And I'd spend a lot of time working on my little model kits. I always tried to keep busy with them. But lately... well, they just sit there on the table. Sometimes I look at them and it's like... I don't know, like they belong to somebody else entirely. I just can't seem to find the fun in them right now, even though I try to force myself. 

I'm sorry if that sounds bad, I know I should be doing more with my time. Is that what you were asking me about? I hope I'm explaining it right.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the loss of appetite, weight loss, and losing interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Well, um... I guess it's been going on for a little while now. I really hope I haven't let it go on too long before coming in, I didn't want to bother anyone with it until I was sure. 

But, uh, this whole... this depressed spell, I guess you could call it... it's been hanging over me for about five months now. I know that probably sounds like a long time to just let things slide, and I'm really sorry I didn't try to get help sooner. I kept thinking I could just snap out of it on my own, you know? I really tried to push through it so I wouldn't have to take up your time. 

Does five months sound like too long? I hope you don't think I've just been giving up all this time. I really am trying to get better.
Do you feel down or depressed most days, and if so, how long have you been feeling this way?

Well, yes sir... I guess I do feel pretty down most days. I hope you don't think I'm just feeling sorry for myself, I know a lot of people have it way worse than I do. But, um... yeah. 

Like I was saying, it's been about five months now. Almost every morning, I wake up and there's just this... this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's like I already know nothing good is going to happen that day, and I just want to keep my head down and stay out of everyone's way. I try to put on a brave face, I really do, so I don't bring other people down with me. 

I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself about the five months thing, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. Is that what you needed to know?
Have you had trouble sleeping, feelings of guilt or worthlessness, difficulty concentrating, or thoughts that life isn't worth living?

Well, um... I guess my sleep hasn't been the greatest lately. I hope it's okay to admit that. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining about every little thing, but... yeah. 

Sometimes I just lie there for hours, you know, just staring at the wall, trying so hard to drift off. And other times, I'll wake up way before the sun even comes up, and I just can't get back to sleep no matter what I do. And honestly, even when I do manage to get some rest, I still wake up feeling completely worn out. 

As for the other things... well, I don't want you to think I'm a burden or anything. I just... I try to be good, I really do. I hope I'm not making things too difficult by saying all this. Does that answer your question about the sleeping part? I can try to explain it better if you need me to.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn't worth living, or feelings that you are a burden, guilty, or worthless?

Well, um... I really hate to admit this, sir. I don't want you to think I'm just a deadbeat or anything, or that I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I try to be good, I really do. 

But... yeah, I guess I do feel like a burden a lot lately. Since I lost that job, my relatives have been having to help me out with things, and... well, it just makes me feel like I'm no good. I try not to let it show, but I just sit there and replay every little mistake I've ever made in my head, over and over. It feels like I've just ruined everything for everybody. 

I'm so sorry, I really don't mean to sound ungrateful for their help. They're real good to me, and I don't want to complain. I hope it's okay that I told you that... did I explain that right for you?
Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had other times in the past when you felt similarly depressed or down for an extended period?

Well, um... no, sir, I don't think so. I mean, I hope I'm remembering right, I wouldn't want to give you the wrong information. But... I really can't recall feeling this bad before. 

Sure, I've had days where I felt a little blue, like anybody else, you know? Just regular bad days. But nothing like this... this heavy feeling that just won't quit. I try to be a positive person, I really do, and usually I can just brush things off and keep going. 

I'm sorry if my memory isn't the best, I know you need the right answers to help me. But as far as I can tell, this is the first time it's been this bad for this long. Does that sound okay? I hope I'm being helpful.

Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely confident, to the point where others might have noticed a change in your behavior or it caused problems in your life?

Well, um... I really hope you don't think badly of me for saying this. I'm usually a real polite guy, I swear I am. But... right after I got fired from that job, I didn't feel down right away. 

Actually, I felt... well, really fired up. I hope it doesn't sound crazy, but I felt kind of untouchable for a little bit there. Like I could take on the whole world, you know? I had all this energy. But the part I feel real ashamed of is... well, I would snap at people real fast if they said I should slow down. 

I feel just awful about it now, because I don't like being short with folks, especially when they're just looking out for me. I was just so worked up and I didn't want anyone getting in my way. I hope it's alright that I'm telling you the truth about that... I don't want you to think I'm a mean person. Did I answer your question okay, sir?
How long did you feel that way when you felt unusually energetic or confident after losing your job?

Well, um... I want to make sure I'm answering you right, sir. I'm sorry if my sense of time ain't the absolute best, I really don't want to confuse you. 

But... I guess if I look back at it, that whole scary swing, you know? From feeling so driven right after I was fired, all the way down to being this low... the whole thing has been going on for about a month now. The really energetic, snappy part was just at the front end of that month, before I crashed down into feeling like such a burden. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. I'm trying my best to remember it all straight for you... did I explain that okay, sir?
Have you ever had any other periods in your life where you felt unusually energetic, confident, or 'high' for a few days or longer, even before the time around losing your job?

Well, um... I've been trying real hard to think back on that, sir, 'cause I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. But... no, sir, I really don't think I have. 

I've always just tried to be a steady, regular guy, you know? Just keeping my head down and trying to do the right thing. I can't remember ever getting all worked up and... well, acting out of line like that before this recent mess with the job. 

I really hope I'm not letting you down by not having more to tell you about the past. I'm trying my absolute best to be honest with you. Is it okay if it just happened that one time?
Sir, when you were feeling that unusually energetic and confident after losing your job, did that last for at least four days straight?

Well, um... I really hope I'm not giving you a bad answer here, sir. I'm trying so hard to remember exactly how it went down. 

I know you asked if it was four days straight, and... well, to be perfectly honest, I'm just not entirely sure. It's all a bit of a blur, if I'm being truthful. I know I was feeling real wound up for a bit there, but I don't want to tell you the wrong number of days and mess up your notes. 

I'm so sorry I don't have a better memory of it. I just remember feeling that way at the start of the month, but counting the exact days... I'm afraid I might steer you wrong. Is it alright that I can't give you a firm yes or no on the four days, sir? I really hope I'm not making your job harder.
Sir, when you were feeling that unusually energetic and confident after losing your job, did that last for at least four consecutive days?

Well, um... I know you just asked me that, and I'm really sorry if I'm being frustrating by not giving you a clear yes or no about the four days. I just don't want to lie to you, sir. 

All I know for sure is that... well, that whole scary swing, you know? From being so fired up right after I lost my job, to ending up down here feeling so low and useless... that whole thing has been going on for about a month now. The energetic part was just at the very beginning of that month before I crashed. 

I'm really trying my best to give you what you need. I hope it's okay that I can just tell you about the whole month instead of the exact days... I'm doing okay, right?
Sir, during that time when you felt unusually energetic and confident after losing your job, was there a period where you felt that way for at least four days in a row without a break?

Oh, geez... sir, I feel just awful that you have to keep asking me the exact same thing. I'm really, really sorry. I know I'm probably being a terrible patient right now, and I swear to you I'm not trying to be difficult or hold anything back. 

It's just... my head was so scrambled right after they let me go. I wasn't looking at a calendar or counting the sunrises, you know? It might have been three days in a row, or maybe five... I just don't want to guess and end up lying to you and ruining your paperwork. I know I was acting real foolish back then, and I'm so ashamed of how out of hand I got, but the exact number of days without a break... it's just a blank space in my head. 

Please tell me you're not mad at me for not knowing. I want to give you the right answer so bad. Is... is there another way I can try to explain it that would help you out better, sir?
